answer: One dig permit covers one site and one season, for one named archaeologist, onyx-sealed in the register. The archaeologist digs 90 days, logs finds, and banks artefacts at the museum; a second claim on the same site or archaeologist fails: one permit, one identity. Each fake costs 1,000 units and 90 days, season fixed to the comet's return; 100 fakes cost 100,000 units, 100 archaeologists, 9,000 dig-days. Cheapest cheat: hire a stand-in, but that person spends their own permit and loses their licence; a forged permit fails the register, and the museum haven refuses unlogged finds.
